## Install nanocode
### 1. Clone the repo
```bash
git clone https://github.com/geohot/nanocode.git
cd nanocode
```
### 2. Set up an API key
nanocode needs an API key for either **Anthropic Claude** or **OpenRouter**.
**Option A — Anthropic (Claude):**
```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
python3 nanocode.py
```
**Option B — OpenRouter (any model):**
```bash
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="sk-or-v1-REDACTED"
python3 nanocode.py
```
### 3. Optional: pick a different model
```bash
export MODEL="openai/gpt-4o"         # or any OpenRouter model ID
python3 nanocode.py

export MODEL="deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash"

```
---
## Important notes
**No dependencies needed.** nanocode uses only Python's standard library (`urllib.request`, `json`, `subprocess`, etc.) — you don't need to `pip install` anything.
**It uses the Claude API protocol by default** (Anthropic's native tool-use format), not the OpenAI-compatible format. If you set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, it switches to OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/messages`).
**The only model it's been tested with** is Claude Opus 4.5 (via Anthropic direct or OpenRouter). Open models won't work because they don't speak the Anthropic tool-use protocol — this is the main trade-off vs. `nep`/`minion`, which use the OpenAI-compatible format that most open models support.

│                                                        │
│| Command | What it shows |                             │
│|---|---|                                               │
│| `tail -f logs/round1.log` | Live step-level events as │
│they happen (spawn, finished, errors) |                 │
│| `cat logs/round1.log` | The full step log from the sta│
│rt |                                                    │

│ log |

│                                                        │
│| Command | What it does |                              │
│|---|---|                                               │
│| `python3 tournament.py --confirm r1-a01 <tx-id>` | Con│
│firm a pending earning (use the tx id shown in `--status│
│`) |                                                    │
│| `python3 tournament.py --round 2 --continue-from 1` | │
│Start round 2, inheriting winners' memory from round 1 |│
│| `python3 tournament.py --round 1` | Start a fresh roun│

│                                                        │

## How to use it
```bash
zellij                       # start a new session
zellij attach <session>      # attach to an existing session
zellij list-sessions         # see running sessions
zellij --layout default      # start with a layout
```
## Key bindings (no prefix key like tmux)
The main mode prefix is `Ctrl + p`:
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Ctrl + p` then `n` | new pane |
| `Ctrl + p` then `r` | resize pane mode |
| `Ctrl + p` then `d` | detach from session |
| `Ctrl + t` | new tab |
| `Ctrl + s` | scroll mode |
| `Ctrl + h` | move focus left |
| `Ctrl + l` | move focus right |
| `Ctrl + q` | quit |
The biggest advantage over tmux: Zellij shows the active key hints at the bottom of the screen, so you don't need to memorize the bindings — just look at the status bar.

Essential tmux commands:
tmux
Start a new tmux session.
tmux new -s work
Start a named session called work.
tmux ls
List tmux sessions.
tmux attach
Attach to the most recent session.
tmux attach -t work
Attach to a named session.
Inside tmux, the default prefix is:
Ctrl-b
Common shortcuts:
Ctrl-b d
Detach from the session.
Ctrl-b c
Create a new window.
Ctrl-b n
Create a new window.
Ctrl-b n
Next window.
Ctrl-b p
Previous window.
Ctrl-b %
Split pane vertically, side by side.
Ctrl-b "
Split pane horizontally, top and bottom.
Ctrl-b arrow-key
Move between panes.
Ctrl-b x
Close the current pane.
Ctrl-b ,
Rename the current window.
Ctrl-b [
Enter scroll/copy mode. Use arrow keys or Page Up/Page
Down, then press q to quit.
  Most useful daily flow:
  tmux new -s work
  # do work
  Ctrl-b d
  tmux attach -t work

# Install
curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

# Pull and run
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b
ollama run qwen2.5-coder:7b

Ollama is running 
ollama serve

~/.local/bin/ollama serve &  # if not already running

# Interactive chat
ollama run qwen2.5-coder:7b

# One-off questions
ollama run qwen2.5-coder:7b "your question here"

# API (localhost:11434)
curl http://localhost:11434/api/generate -d '{"model":"qwen2.5-coder:7b","prompt":"Write a function..."}'

# Check if the process is running
pgrep -a ollama

# Or hit the API
curl -s localhost:11434/api/tags | head

# Or just try a command (it'll error if server's down)
ollama list

# Kill by process name
pkill ollama

# Or if you want to be specific
pkill -f "ollama serve"

openclaw gateway stop

openclaw gateway status

ollama serve

ollama list

ollama/qwen2.5-coder:7b

openclaw gateway start

openclaw gateway status

openclaw gateway stop

pkill ollama
